newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark says no inkling of NZ First choice.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark says no inkling of NZ First choice.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark said on Monday those who saw a greater likelihood of a National Party government coming from the current coalition talks had no basis for their belief.
"They are not in the room and they haven't got a clue," Clark said as she entered the latest round of talks with NZ First. She said she had no inkling whatsoever of which way NZ First would jump.

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is holding talks with centre-left Labour and the incumbent conservative National government over the shape of the next government.

Asked how she interpreted NZ First leader Winston Peters' comments on Sunday that a large number of his supporters would be disappointed by his choice, Clark said: "I think if you are speaking to an audience in Tauranga of NZ First supporters, most of whom are former National voters, you would make that point." Tauranga is Peters' home constituency.
Clark said time was passing for a deal to be struck. "The clock's ticking on."

She said if no deal was struck by December 13 when parliament must meet, the caretaker National government would keep going and there would be little business other than the election of a speaker, who chairs parliament, and the swearing in of MPs.
"I think the country has got a sense of impatience. We are just going to conduct the negotiations with as much dignity as possible in the circumstances," Clark said.

"I am not aware of a great list of urgent matters to be dealt with. The country normally goes to sleep over the summer in any case so whether the consequences (of the caretaker government continuing) are major remains to be seen."
She said no time had been set down for further talks with the left-wing Alliance "but I am sure we will be talking to them this week".
An NZ First-Labour government would need the support of the 13 left-wing Alliance MPs to be assured a majority in the 120 seat parliament. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
